text:
objective: To examine decadal Land Use Land Cover (LULC) changes from 1990 to 2020 and simulate future LULC for 2030 and 2050 under different scenarios for Taiwan, incorporating demographic factors.
country: Taiwan
land_use_classes: Barren; Uncultivated; Shallow Water; Deep Water; Built-up; Forest; Cultivated
baseline_years: 1990; 2000; 2010; 2020
target_future_years: 2030; 2050
scenarios: 2-variables; 3-variables; 5-variables; 6-variables
analysis_methods: Maximum Likelihood Classifier (supervised classification); Support Vector Machine (SVM); Markov-chain model; SVM-Markov chain model; Accuracy assessment (confusion matrix, Kappa coefficient, Producer's Accuracy, User's Accuracy, Overall Accuracy, RMSE); Transition potential modeling
simulation_method_advantages: The integration of SVM classification with Markov-chain modeling enables precise LULC classification and dynamic land-cover predictions. SVM provides high classification accuracy, and the Markov-chain model predicts future changes based on historical transition probabilities. This hybrid approach improves accuracy in complex urban landscapes and is one of the first applications at a national scale for Taiwan.
predictors: Aspect; Elevation; Hillshade; Distance to river; Distance to road; Slope
population_selected: Yes
data_sources: Landsat series satellite images (Landsat 5, 7, 8 Surface Reflectance Tier 1); SRTM-Digital Elevation Model (30 m); Open Street Maps; Google Earth
tools_software_used: Google Earth Engine
validation_performed: Yes
validation_methods: Confusion matrix; Kappa coefficient; Producer's Accuracy; User's Accuracy; Overall Accuracy; RMSE (Root-Mean-Square-Error)
validation_data_sources: Ground Control Points (GCPs) - 655 points for historical classification validation, 300 points for 2020 simulation validation
key_findings: Built-up area increased by 140% from 1990 to 2020; Under the 6-variables scenario, built-up area is projected to increase by 223% from 1990 by 2050; Barren land decreased by 49.17% from 1990 to 2020; Forest area increased by 2.19% from 1990 to 2020; Cultivated land increased by 15.27% from 1990 to 2020; The 3-variables scenario (Elevation, Distance to roads, Distance to rivers) was identified as the best for simulation, providing results similar to the 6-variables scenario with fewer inputs; The simulated LULC for 2020 validation achieved an overall accuracy of 0.87 and a Kappa index of 0.74.
implications: The study provides essential information for urban planning, infrastructure development, and environmental conservation. The combination of negative population growth and increasing impervious surfaces presents a significant topic for sustainable land-use strategy development. Findings can aid in mitigating negative environmental impacts and planning for public needs.
limitations: Satellite images before 1990 were not considered due to high cloud coverage; The Markov model assumes stationary transition probabilities, which may not hold under rapid policy or environmental shifts; The model does not incorporate external drivers like socio-economic factors or policy changes; Accuracy was lower for the 1990 dataset (Overall Accuracy=0.68).
future_directions: Inclusion of socio-economic parameters and other influencing factors like distance to city and population density for specific city or regional studies; Application of the model to other regions with similar rapid urbanization and demographic shifts.
scalability: The national-scale approach and methodology are applicable to other rapidly urbanizing, mid-sized economies with diverse land uses and complex socio-ecological contexts. The integration of ML classification with CA-Markov models provides a model for future studies in similar regions.
novelty: First study to conduct LULC classification and simulation for the complete Taiwan island from 1990 to 2050; Incorporates Taiwan's demographic shifts, including negative population growth, in modeling; Integrates SVM classification with Markov-chain modeling for LULC simulation at a national scale; Provides decadal projections with long-term simulation up to 2050 under multiple scenarios.
